recognize_zh: 周邊血液中數顆淋巴球核深染、染色質濃縮，核輪廓有溝紋與皺褶，呈腦迴狀（cerebriform），胞質極少，其中一顆核拉長呈雙葉，符合 Sézary 細胞。
features: Several small to intermediate lymphocytes with hyperchromatic nuclei
Nuclear grooves and folds producing a convoluted, cerebriform contour
Scant to minimal pale cytoplasm, high N:C ratio
One cell with an elongated, bilobed nucleus; background red cells unremarkable
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows several small to intermediate-sized lymphocytes with hyperchromatic, condensed chromatin and convoluted nuclear contours with grooves and folds, imparting a cerebriform appearance. Cytoplasm is scant and nucleoli are not seen; one cell has an elongated bilobed nucleus. Red cells and platelets are unremarkable. Findings are consistent with circulating Sézary cells; diagnosis of Sézary syndrome requires erythroderma, lymphadenopathy and flow cytometry showing a clonal CD4+ T-cell population with loss of CD7 and/or CD26 (at least 1000/µL).

ddx.vs: ATLL cells are flower cells with multilobated petal-like nuclei, associated with HTLV-1 and hypercalcemia, rather than fine cerebriform folds.
T-PLL cells have a visible nucleolus and cytoplasmic blebs, with marked lymphocytosis and TCL1A rearrangement.
Occasional reactive cells with nuclear folds occur in benign erythroderma, but lack a clonal TCR rearrangement and CD7/CD26 loss.
